scope: Proposition 9.2 of the manuscript “A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal's function” (preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 021 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f80267eebc82a9b8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 56. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the compact-box parameters, the inverse-estimate parameters and a relative-error threshold ε > 0. For every fixed σ2 > 0 there is a fixed sufficiently large Cs, independent of sufficiently small fixed ξ, with the following property. For every candidate box, every choice of its factors other than the isolated prime, and every rational on its fixed candidate list for which (9.1) holds, suppose T > wCs . For sufficiently large z, fewer than σ2np primes p ∈ P both align to A/D and satisfy |Npqf /µpqf − 1| > ε. The estimate is uniform in the box, the fixed prime choices, the rational and the forbidden classes. The threshold on z may depend on fixed ξ. The fraction is measured against all primes of P.
